title: Chat Languages Models missing
content: I have Github Copilot Chat running in VS Code and I have added OpenRouter provider to my Copilot and after using it, I have added few other Custom Endpoint chat completion Providers to the Languages Model, I have been using two of the other Custom Endpoint providers for about 3 to 4 days after that suddenly the OpenRouters Models is missing in the models list. I couldn't able to see them. I have checked chatLanguageModels.json file the OpenRouter vendor is exists, and checked Language Models Page (Copilot Chat Extension's) I couldn't able to other providers (including OpenRouter) i could see only the last used added two Custom Endpoint vendors only. I tried to add OpenRouter again by clicking on Add Model Button and selected OpenRouter Provider directly it suggests the name OpenRouter 2 as Provider name and shows warning if I type only OpenRouter as error "A Language models group with this name already exists". I tried as testing purpose even after the error when I click on enter it still asks me API key without rejecting that action but after entering the API key it doesn't reflect the change(that's good) but even though I tried to close and relaunch, disable and enable the extensions nothing is happening or changing still I couldn't that other providers list, but when I add another provider as new like OpenRouter 2 and then I could see that newly added Provider models only. what's this Issue. why it's happening. I also found another issue like when I opened VS Code without connecting to Internet and then later on connected to Internet and try to Prompt and start conversation with other Provider the connection and generation isn't happening with that provider rather it is using copilot models and generating the output. Both these Issues found in different times and testing multiple times, not once. So Please verify this issues and fix these bugs. - Copilot Chat Extension Version: v0.58.0 - VS Code Version: v1.130.0 - OS Version: Windows 10 - Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agent (not related to this bug issue) - Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Custom Endpoints and Openrouter Models Steps to Reproduce (for Bug 1: Models Missing): 1. Try to add different Provider in Language Models and then use that Model only for a day 2. Then Try add few other Provider models like 2 to 4 different Providers or Else custom endpoints 3. Then Use newly added Provider models only ( I have used them 3 days and more) 4. After then You won't able to see those previously created in first Provider in the Language Models List and Models won't appear anywhere. I can produce the screenshots on what exactly you would like to see, My suggestion is to please add Copilot Chat extension a refresh or restart extension button and also Remap or reload entire Models list from chatLanguageModels.json file in Language Models Page. whatever the models I see in this Language Models Page is viewing in the Github chat Model selection so I couldn't able to view all the models completely. --- Steps to Reproduce (for Bug 2: Copilot running its native models or Auto Model): 1. Turn of Your WIFI or Internet Connection and Open VS Code 2. Let it load everything or else open directly Copilot chat. 3. Now connect to Internet and Open the chat session previously had, then select different Model Provider other than Copilot Models or Auto Mode (I'm Using Agent Mode in my chat and used an Custom Endpoint Provider) 4. Give anything Prompt to work or execute your task. You'll be seeing the Copilot Model executing the task than your chosen Model and provider. 5. To work again we have to close and reopen the entire VS Code IDE. Attaching the Bug 2 Screenshot:

title: Can't update API key if I don't have more than one provider
content: Type: Feature Request So basically I found out that I cannot update the API key of a provider for VS code chat if I don't have multiple ones because it won't show me the grouping which I can then select the settings for if I only had one I don't have an active subscription so maybe this is why it's not showing me the groups because the only group that I have is open router the only way I was able to fix this is by just trying to create another group for open router and when I did that it actually showed me the grouping which allowed me to edit the settings of the previous one to update the API key So keep this in mind because it was really frustrating and I've only accidentally stumbled on this solution by accident VS Code version: Code 1.130.0 (1b6a188127eeaf9194f945eb6eb89a657e93c54c, 2026-07-22T14:55:04Z) OS version: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200 Modes:

title: Git "merge/save with conflicts" modal dialogs get blocked, UI becomes unresponsive
content:
Type: Bug When a modal dialog appears, it prevents usage of VScode even when the modal is not visible. Code doesn't seem to care if the dialog is visible. The dialog may even appear on a different desktop. When I use the Git Merge / Conflict resolution and I try to close the window with conflicts still unresolved, Code displays a modal dialog asking if I'm sure I want to quit/save. But if there's another modal dialog already open, the merge dialog doesn't get displayed. Code becomes unresponsive to most GUI inputs for the merge editor. In some cases, I have a separate Code instance on a different desktop. It has displayed a modal telling me it cannot connect to my Remote SSH Host and asking if I want to retry/cancel or something. I haven't looked at that instance in hours or days. Now when I try to close my Merge editor with conflicts, it freezes. After some experimentation, I eventually figured out there was a modal open on another desktop for another instance. When I dismissed that modal, my Merge modal dialog finally appeared, even though it was for the other instance on the other desktop. title: VS Code 1.129 crashes on launch with error code 135 on NVIDIA GPU + Wayland
content:
Description

VS Code crashes immediately upon launch with error code 135 on Linux (Wayland session). The crash does not occur in version 1.128. Using --ozone-platform=x11 resolves the issue while keeping GPU acceleration active. The system is running Wayland with an NVIDIA GPU.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Install VS Code version 1.129.0-1784074987

  2. Launch VS Code normally: code

  3. VS Code crashes with the error dialog: "The window terminated unexpectedly (reason: 'crashed', code: '135')"

Expected Behavior

VS Code should launch normally without crashing.

Actual Behavior

VS Code crashes immediately with error code 135.

Workarounds

  • code --disable-gpu - works but disables GPU acceleration

  • code --ozone-platform=x11 - works and keeps GPU acceleration active ✅

System Information

title: Linux Pasting file from Nautilus only shows filename or "/" instead of full path
content:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting bugs and suggestions: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with it. -->

- VS Code Version: 1.123.0 (also tested on 1.122.1)
- OS Version: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, GNOME Shell 46.0, X11 (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11`)
- Hardware: x86_64

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open Nautilus (GNOME Files) file manager
2. Select any file and press `Ctrl+C` (or right-click → Copy)
3. Switch to VS Code editor and press `Ctrl+V`
4. Instead of the full file path (e.g., `/home/user/Documents/test.pdf`), only the filename (`test.pdf`) or just `/` is pasted

---

## Root Cause Analysis

When a file is copied in Nautilus, the system clipboard contains **three MIME types**:

| MIME Type | Content |
|---|---|
| `text/uri-list` | `file:///home/user/Documents/test.pdf` ✅ full path (URL-encoded) |
| `text/plain` | `test.pdf` ❌ filename only |
| `x-special/gnome-copied-files` | `copy\nfile:///home/user/Documents/test.pdf` (GNOME internal) |

**Old VS Code behavior**: Read `text/uri-list`, decoded the `file://` URI, and inserted the full path as text.

**Current VS Code behavior** (1.122.x / 1.123.x): Reads `text/plain`, which only contains the filename.

I verified this by checking the clipboard with `xclip`:
```
$ xclip -selection clipboard -t text/uri-list -o
file:///home/user/Documents/test.pdf

$ xclip -selection clipboard -t text/plain -o
test.pdf
```

The `text/uri-list` data is present and correct, but VS Code ignores it.

## Attempted Fixes (none worked)

1. `"files.copyFilesAsText": true` — only controls copy behavior inside VS Code, not paste from external apps
2. `"editor.pasteAs.enabled": false` — disables the paste-as feature but VS Code still reads `text/plain`
3. `"editor.pasteAs.preferences": ["text.plain"]` — limits MIME type selection but doesn't change which format is read
4. Downgraded from 1.123.0 to 1.122.1 — behavior changed from `/` to filename, still not full path
5. `"editor.dropIntoEditor.enabled": false` — no effect on paste behavior

## Workaround

I created a small VS Code extension (`nautilus-clipboard-fix`) that:
1. Polls the clipboard every 300ms using `xclip -selection clipboard -t text/uri-list -o`
2. When a `file://` URI is detected, decodes it to a local path and caches it
3. Intercepts `Ctrl+V` — if a cached path exists, inserts it as text; otherwise falls back to normal paste

This confirms the issue is purely in VS Code's clipboard reading logic: the `text/uri-list` data is available on the clipboard, but VS Code's Electron clipboard API on Linux reads `text/plain` instead.

## Related Issues

- #170708 — Cannot paste full file paths after copying file from file explorer on Linux
- #147285 — Copy/paste file path from the file explorer is not working
- #155453 — File path not pasted from file manager in Linux

## Suggested Fix

When pasting from an external file manager on Linux, VS Code should:
1. Check if `text/uri-list` contains `file://` URIs
2. If yes, decode them to local paths and insert as text
3. Only fall back to `text/plain` if no `file://` URIs are found

This would restore the behavior that worked in older versions and matches what most Linux users expect.

- VS Code Version: 1.130.0 (Universal), Commit 1b6a188127eeaf9194f945eb6eb89a657e93c54c, 2026-07-22T14:55:04Z, Electron 42.6.0, Chromium 148.0.7778.280, Node.js 24.18.0
- OS Version: Darwin arm64 27.0.0 (macOS pre-release)

All GPT-5.6 models (Sol, Terra) fail on macOS with an empty error object.
GPT-5.5 and older models work in the same window, same session.
The same GitHub account with the same VS Code version works on Windows.
This has persisted across the last two VS Code updates.

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Open Copilot Chat on macOS, Ask mode
2. Select GPT-5.6 Sol (or Terra)
3. Send "test" -> request fails immediately
4. Switch to GPT-5.5, send "test" -> works

Error:
Sorry, your request failed. Please try again.
Reason: {"code":0,"message":"","metadata":{}}: Error: {"code":0,"message":"","metadata":{}}
  at jG._provideLanguageModelResponse
  (/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:1690:14392)
  at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:104:5)
  at async jG.provideLanguageModelResponse
  (/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:1690:15357)

Client Request Ids:
- 34e0c908-aa94-4771-96b7-c322b332e577
- c8617b33-decf-4f44-a8da-b796e2d9b9ff
- 4bab8901-d1a3-40c8-b760-0d4c86b15a8f
- 8317d7f7-b3a2-4c73-bd99-df6caf5c8141

Log (GitHub Copilot Chat output channel):
ccreq:755215d9.copilotmd | failed | gpt-5.6-sol | 2665ms | [copilotLanguageModelWrapper]
[ToolCallingLoop] Stop hook result: shouldContinue=false, reasons=undefined

Note the 2665ms: the request reaches the backend and is rejected server-side.
The rejection reason is not surfaced to the client.

Plan: Copilot Max.
Second machine: Windows, same account, same VS Code version -> GPT-5.6 Sol works.

Already ruled out:
- Extensions: reproduced with --disable-extensions
- Auth: other models work with the same token; sign out / sign in unchanged
- Tools / MCP: fails in Ask mode with no tools enabled
- Workspace / custom instructions: fails in an empty window with no folder open
- Client version: identical on the working Windows machine
- Reload Window
- Cache: deleted globalStorage/github.copilot-chat and CachedData
- Quota: additional budget still available, and the same account works on Windows

Expected: either the request succeeds, or the client surfaces the actual
rejection reason instead of an empty {"code":0,"message":""}.

title: Feature Request: Allow specifying reasoning effort per subagent invocation
content:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

Currently, the `runSubagent` tool (used by chat agents / extensions to delegate tasks to sub-agents) does not expose a parameter to control the **reasoning effort** (thinking budget) of the spawned subagent. The only way to influence reasoning effort is through the global session-level setting or the upcoming "efficiency mode" toggle (#320470).

This is insufficient for real-world orchestration scenarios where a single session spawns multiple subagents with **very different complexity requirements**:

| Task delegated to subagent | Ideal effort |
|---|---|
| Simple file search / grep | `low` |
| One-shot code generation from a known pattern | `low` or `medium` |
| Complex multi-step analysis or architecture decision | `high` |
| Research across multiple files with synthesis | `high` |

A global toggle forces an all-or-nothing trade-off — either all subagents burn maximum tokens, or all are constrained.

## Proposed Solution

Allow specifying reasoning effort **per subagent call**, with two complementary surfaces:

### Option A: `reasoningEffort` parameter on the `runSubagent` tool

```jsonc
{
  "prompt": "...",
  "model": "Claude Opus 4.6 (copilot)",
  "reasoningEffort": "high"   // "high" | "medium" | "low"
}
```

This gives the orchestrating agent (or extension) dynamic, per-call control.

### Option B: Declarative default in `.agent.md` frontmatter

```yaml
---
tools: [...]
reasoningEffort: low
---
```

This lets agent authors set a sensible default for their agent's typical workload, while still allowing per-call override via Option A.

## Benefits

- **Cost optimization**: Low-effort subagents for trivial lookups save significant tokens/credits without degrading quality on complex tasks.
- **Latency**: Lower effort → faster responses for simple delegations.
- **Composability**: Power users and extension authors can build efficient multi-agent workflows with fine-grained control.
- **Complementary to #320470**: The global efficiency mode sets a floor; per-subagent effort allows targeted overrides.

## Related

- #320470 — Explore an "efficiency mode" selection for chat (mentions "low reasoning for subagents" as part of global mode)

title: Delayed Python environment auto-activation can corrupt active terminal input
content:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->

The Python extension appears to inject the virtual environment activation command into the integrated terminal after the terminal has already become interactive.

If the user starts typing, pasting, or browsing/editing shell history immediately after opening a terminal, the activation command can be inserted into the active prompt buffer and become part of the user’s command.

For example, a user may open a terminal, begin entering a command, and then VS Code injects something like:

`source /path/to/project/.venv/bin/activate`

This can result in a corrupted command such as:

`some user command source /path/to/project/.venv/bin/activate`

### Actual behavior

The activation command may be inserted into the current interactive shell input after the user has already begun interacting with the terminal.

### Expected behavior

VS Code should not inject text into an interactive terminal once the user has started entering or editing input.

Safer behavior could include:

performing activation before the terminal becomes interactive;
cancelling activation if the user has typed anything;
checking that the prompt buffer is empty before injecting;

## Impact

This can unexpectedly execute harmful commands. It is also difficult to diagnose because it can appear as if the shell or command history is malfunctioning.

## Workaround

Disable automatic terminal environment activation:
```json
"python.terminal.activateEnvironment": false
```

title: Fix false hydration mismatch when client renders portal that returned null on server
content:
## Summary

Fixes #12615

When a component returns `null` on the server but renders a `ReactDOM.createPortal()` on the client, React was incorrectly emitting a hydration mismatch error:

```
Hydration failed because the server rendered HTML didn't match the client.
  <span>
    <HoverMenu>
+     <div>   ← false positive: this is portal content, not a span child
```

This is a false positive — the portal's `<div>` renders into a **separate container**, not into the parent `<span>`. It should not be compared against the parent's server HTML.

## Root Cause

When `updatePortalComponent` calls `pushHostContainer` to switch to the portal's container, the hydration state variables (`isHydrating`, `nextHydratableInstance`, `hydrationParentFiber`) were not reset. The portal's children then tried to claim hydration instances from the **parent container's** server nodes, which failed and triggered a mismatch error.

## Fix

Added two functions to `ReactFiberHydrationContext`:

- **`prepareToHydrateHostPortal`** — called in `updatePortalComponent` (begin work). Saves the current hydration state onto a stack and resets it, so portal children are inserted fresh rather than matched against server HTML.
- **`popHydrationStateAfterPortal`** — called in the `HostPortal` case of complete work. Restores the saved hydration state so the parent resumes hydrating correctly after the portal.

This correctly handles nested portals (via the stack) and cleans up on `resetHydrationState` (work loop interruption).

## Test Plan

- Added two new tests in `ReactDOMHydrationDiff-test.js`:
  - Portal renders to a separate container → no mismatch warning
  - Portal renders to the hydration root container → no mismatch warning
- All 39 hydration diff tests pass
- All 183 tests across `ReactServerRenderingHydration`, `ReactDOMServerPartialHydration`, and `ReactDOMFiber` suites pass

title: [compiler] Fix refs validation for forwarded ref props
content:
Fixes #35997

## Summary

This fixes a false positive in `react-hooks/refs` when forwarding a `ref` prop directly to JSX.

Previously, code like:

```tsx
function TextArea(props) {
  return <TextInput ref={props.ref} type="body" />;
}
```

was reported as:

`Cannot access refs during render`

even though the component was only forwarding the ref object to JSX and not reading `ref.current`.

The root cause was that `ValidateNoRefAccessInRender` validated all JSX attribute operands uniformly. That was too strict for the special `ref` prop, where passing a ref object through to JSX should be allowed.

This change teaches the validator to treat JSX `ref` attributes specially:

- still validate the JSX tag
- still validate non-`ref` JSX attributes
- still validate spread attributes and children
- skip direct-ref-value validation for the `ref` attribute itself

This preserves the existing error for actual render-time ref reads like `props.ref.current`, while allowing valid ref forwarding patterns.

## How did you test this change?

Reproduced the issue with a focused compiler fixture:

1. Add a fixture containing:

```js
// @validateRefAccessDuringRender @compilationMode:"infer"
function TextArea(props) {
  return <TextInput ref={props.ref} type="body" />;
}
```

2. Run:

```bash
corepack yarn workspace babel-plugin-react-compiler snap --pattern allow-forwarding-ref-prop-to-jsx --sync
```

Before the fix, this failed with:

```text
Error: Cannot access refs during render
...
return <TextInput ref={props.ref} type="body" />;
                         ^^^^^^^^^ Cannot access ref value during render
```

After the fix, the same targeted fixture passes:

```bash
corepack yarn workspace babel-plugin-react-compiler snap --pattern allow-forwarding-ref-prop-to-jsx --sync
```

I also checked the existing invalid fixture for reading `props.ref.current` to confirm the validator still rejects direct ref-value access during render.

title: [Flight] Performance track debug info is not recovered for plain object roots
content:
## Summary

`flushComponentPerformance` reads `root._debugInfo` from the chunk. When
that array is empty and the chunk is fulfilled, it recovers the debug info
from the resolved value, but only when the value is an array, an async
iterable, a React element, or a lazy:

```js
if (debugInfo.length === 0 && root.status === 'fulfilled') {
  const resolvedValue = resolveLazy(root.value);
  if (
    typeof resolvedValue === 'object' && resolvedValue !== null &&
    (isArray(resolvedValue) ||
      typeof resolvedValue[ASYNC_ITERATOR] === 'function' ||
      resolvedValue.$$typeof === REACT_ELEMENT_TYPE ||
      resolvedValue.$$typeof === REACT_LAZY_TYPE) &&
    isArray(resolvedValue._debugInfo)
  ) {
    debugInfo = resolvedValue._debugInfo;
  }
}
```

A plain object root is excluded, so the Server Components track in the
Performance panel does not work for payloads whose root is a plain object,
even when the resolved value carries a `_debugInfo` array. Verified in
`react-server-dom-webpack@19.3.0-canary-28cd4bb0-20260723`.

## Context

Waku's RSC payload root is a plain object mapping slot ids to elements
(`Record<string, unknown>`), which lets one payload carry several named
elements. This shape is deliberate and we would like to keep it. Today we
patch the read site with a build transform that drops the type restriction,
which works but is coupled to the compiled output:

https://github.com/wakujs/waku/blob/main/packages/waku/src/lib/vite-plugins/patch-rsdw.ts

@vitejs/plugin-rsc documents the same shape constraint for its performance
track example (vitejs/vite-plugin-react#1152, vitejs/vite-plugin-react#1304).

## Request

Relax the recovery to accept any object value that carries an own
`_debugInfo` array. The type restriction seems to mirror
`moveDebugInfoFromChunkToInnerValue`, where it guards attaching
`_debugInfo` to the value. The read site only reads the property, so the
restriction does not appear to protect anything there, and the relaxation
is additive: values without `_debugInfo` behave as before.

If there is a supported way to get the performance track with a plain
object root without reshaping the payload, that guidance would also
resolve this for us.

title: Bump axios from 1.7.7 to 1.18.1 in /compiler/apps/playground
content:
Bumps [axios](https://github.com/axios/axios) from 1.7.7 to 1.18.1.
Release notes

Sourced from axios's releases.

v1.18.1 — June 21, 2026

This release focuses on Node HTTP adapter fixes, safer AxiosError serialisation, runtime/type correctness fixes, documentation updates, and dependency maintenance.

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • AxiosError Serialisation: Made AxiosError#cause non-enumerable to prevent circular JSON serialisation failures when errors include nested causes. (#10913)
  • Node HTTP Adapter: Guarded socket.setKeepAlive for proxy agent streams, accepted path-only URLs when socketPath is configured, deferred environment proxy handling to Node, and explicitly passed maxBodyLength through to follow-redirects. (#10917, #10930, #10942, #10993)
  • Runtime and Type Correctness: Fixed several runtime crashes, type definition mismatches, and incorrect error handling paths. (#10959, #11021)
  • AxiosURLSearchParams: Switched the encoder callback to an arrow function so encoder.call(this) receives the AxiosURLSearchParams instance correctly. (#11019)

🔧 Maintenance & Chores

  • Documentation: Documented sensitive headers and status transition behaviour, prepared cleaned-up docs, added Deno install instructions, and clarified that request data is request-specific (#11007, #11010, #11023, #11025)

  • Dependencies: Bumped vite, rollup, form-data, js-yaml, and multer across the root project, docs, smoke tests, and module test workspaces. (#11011, #11012, #11013, #11014, #11015, #11016, #11017, #11026)

🌟 New Contributors

title: [verified] fix(reconciler): recheck store snapshot after subscribe
content:
## Summary
- Problem: `useSyncExternalStore` can miss a post-subscribe snapshot repair when `Suspense` + `StrictMode` remounts a store consumer and the store mutates during `subscribe()` without notifying listeners.
- Why it matters: the hook contract expects a snapshot re-check after subscribing, but this remount path skipped that repair step.
- What changed: `subscribeToStore(...)` now re-checks the snapshot immediately after `subscribe(handleStoreChange)` returns and forces a rerender if the store changed during subscribe.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): this does not change broader Suspense replay semantics or attempt to guarantee that no stale intermediate render is ever observed before the repair rerender.

## How did you test this change?
- `CI=1 npx -y yarn test useSyncExternalStore-test --runInBand`
- `CI=1 npx -y yarn test useSyncExternalStore --runInBand`

Related to: https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/35550

title: [DOM] Guard window.event reads in scheduler event tracking
content:
## Summary

Fixes #37100.

The DEV-only Performance Tracks instrumentation added in 19.2.0 reads `window.event` unconditionally in `trackSchedulerEvent()`, `resolveEventType()`, and `resolveEventTimeStamp()`. `trackSchedulerEvent()` runs at the entry of Scheduler-driven tasks (`performWorkOnRootViaSchedulerTask`, `processRootScheduleInImmediateTask`, and the passive-effects flush scheduled by `commitRoot`). These tasks live on deferred `setImmediate` ticks and can legitimately fire after a per-test-file DOM environment (jsdom / happy-dom under vitest or jest) has been torn down. When that happens the task throws `ReferenceError: window is not defined` before doing any work, which fails entire CI suites with an unhandled error attributed to the next, innocent test file.

This guards the three reads with `typeof window !== 'undefined'`, matching the bundle's existing convention for `window` accesses that may run outside a browser DOM (e.g. `canUseDOM`, the `window.ErrorEvent` detection in the error-reporting path). When `window` is gone the attribution resolves to `undefined`, i.e. "no event", which is accurate. `shouldAttemptEagerTransition()` and `resolveUpdatePriority()` are left untouched: they only run while an update is being dispatched, so `window` is alive by construction there.

## How did you test this change?

- Added a regression test (`ReactDOMWindowTeardown-test.js`, node environment + manually constructed JSDOM mirroring the issue's repro). It fails on `main` with `ReferenceError: window is not defined` from `performWorkOnRootViaSchedulerTask` and passes with this change.
- `yarn test ReactPerformanceTrack ReactDOMFiberAsync ReactDOMNativeEventHeuristic` — all pass.
- `yarn linc`, `yarn flow dom-node`, `yarn prettier` — clean.
- Ran the repro script from #37100 verbatim: against published `react-dom@19.2.8` it crashes as reported; against a locally built `NODE_DEV` bundle with this change it prints `done, no crash` and exits 0.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [Fiber] Don't reaquire HostSingletons during dev effect validation
content:
Stacked on #37112

In dev effects are validated using a double-invoke technique. To do this the effects are destroyed and recreated during a validation traversal. However this same disappear and reappear path is used when Offscreen Fibers go hidden and HostSingletons have unique behavior when going hidden. So now that the double invoke effects process happens during hydration it is more common to have your Singletons be released and acquired during this validation phase which is observable most notably by having extra attributes removed from them. The prior commits in this stack deal with preserving non-react owned attributes on release however it is semantically incorrect to release and acquire the singleton during this validation because it isn't really an effect, it simply lives in this traversal to avoid having to do another traversal during the commit.

This change adds a bit of info to the release and acquire path to only conditionally perform the necessary reacquire flow if we are not in the validation phase.

title: [Fiber] only remove properties from singletons on release
content:
Removing attributes does not actually reset all property state on the singleton instance. It also has the side effect of wiping any 3rd party set attributes and properties that 3rd party scripts and extensions.

Reimplements the singleton release to clear properties on the instance based on the last committed props for the singleton fiber.

Notably there is an unfixed path with preamble contribution markers that still just clears based on attributes which covers SSR'd attributes that need to be wiped before client recovery on hydration can continue. There are gated failing tests for this as a TODO.

title: [React 19] `use` is significantly slower in some scenarios than throwing a Promise
content:
## Summary

This is something I noticed when I applied the Apollo Client test suite to React 19 - we had one test that was timing out.

I first thought that the test was broken, but it turns out it was just really slow. 

Cranking the test that finished in React 18 in under 200 milliseconds to a timeout of 10 **seconds** for React 19 made it pass (6 seconds would still consistently fail, 7 seconds started to pass on localhost).

Further I noticed that if we use our [`__use`](https://github.com/apollographql/apollo-client/blob/8e3edd4f5e5191453ba3ca1a1cc4fc4a02b936e8/src/react/hooks/internal/__use.ts#L15-L26) polyfill that throws a Promise instead of `use`, the test finishes in under 500 milliseconds - still slower than React 18, but *significantly* faster than React 19 with native `use`.

This is the test in question:

https://github.com/apollographql/apollo-client/blob/8e3edd4f5e5191453ba3ca1a1cc4fc4a02b936e8/src/react/hooks/__tests__/useSuspenseQuery.test.tsx#L9519-L9615

I'd be happy to work with you on further identifying the root cause for this, but I'll be moving houses in a few days, and I just don't have the time to create an isolated reproduction for this within the next 1-2 weeks, I'm really sorry.

Still, I assume this might be important for you, so I'll at least open a ticket to let you know :)

title: os: running SameFile on two character files or pipes will always return true on Windows
content:
### Go version

go version go1.26.4 windows/amd64

### Output of `go env` in your module/workspace:

```shell
set AR=ar
set CC=gcc
set CGO_CFLAGS=-O2 -g
set CGO_CPPFLAGS=
set CGO_CXXFLAGS=-O2 -g

set CGO_FFLAGS=-O2 -g

set GOARCH=amd64
set GOAUTH=netrc
set GOBIN=
set GOCACHE=C:\Users\<REDACTED>\AppData\Local\go-build
set GOCACHEPROG=
set GODEBUG=
set GOENV=C:\Users\<REDACTED>\AppData\Roaming\go\env
set GOEXE=.exe
set GOEXPERIMENT=
set GOFIPS140=off
set GOFLAGS=
set GOGCCFLAGS=-m64 -fno-caret-diagnostics -Qunused-arguments -Wl,--no-gc-sections -fmessage-length=0 -ffile-prefix-map=C:\Users\<REDACTED>\AppData\Local\Temp\go-build3940039365=/tmp/go-build -gno-record-gcc-switches
set GOHOSTARCH=amd64
set GOHOSTOS=windows
set GOINSECURE=
set GOMOD=NUL
set GOMODCACHE=C:\Users\<REDACTED>\go\pkg\mod
set GONOPROXY=
set GONOSUMDB=
set GOOS=windows
set GOPATH=C:\Users\<REDACTED>\go
set GOPRIVATE=
set GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct
set GOROOT=C:\Users\<REDACTED>\scoop\apps\go\current
set GOSUMDB=sum.golang.org
set GOTELEMETRY=local
set GOTELEMETRYDIR=C:\Users\<REDACTED>\AppData\Roaming\go\telemetry
set GOTMPDIR=
set GOTOOLCHAIN=auto
set GOTOOLDIR=C:\Users\<REDACTED>\scoop\apps\go\current\pkg\tool\windows_amd64
set GOVCS=
set GOVERSION=go1.26.4
set GOWORK=
set PKG_CONFIG=pkg-config
```

### What did you do?

```go
package main

import (
   "os"
   "fmt"
)

func main() {
   con, _ := os.Create("CONOUT$")
   defer con.Close()
   
   fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout, "This is stdout")
   fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "This is stderr")
   
   infOut, _ := os.Stdout.Stat()
   infErr, _ := os.Stderr.Stat()
   fmt.Fprintf(con, "Stdout and Stderr are same file: %v\n", os.SameFile(infOut, infErr))
}
```
This was put in a go file and built into an executable called `bugTest.exe` on Windows

### What did you see happen?

This what I see when I run these commands in the Windows command prompt
```
-->bugTest
This is stdout
This is stderr
Stdout and Stderr are same file: true

-->bugTest > nul
This is stderr
Stdout and Stderr are same file: true

-->
```

### What did you expect to see?

If the `os.SameFile` function is run on Windows, and both files are either pipes or character files, the function will always return `true`, even when the files/pipes are different. In the output in the command prompt, the first command invocation works as expected, since both stdout and stderr are direccted to the console, they represent the same file/pipe. But when stdout is redirected to `nul`, the SameFile function still reports `true`, even though stdout is redirected, but stderr still points to the console output.

Here we can see when the `Stat` function is called, if the file type is a character type or a pipe, only the `name` and `filetype` fields of the `fileStat` struct are set

https://github.com/golang/go/blob/03845e30f7b73d1703bd8c21017297f6eecb76d6/src/os/stat_windows.go#L108-L116

Then the `sameFile` function calls `loadFileId` on each `fileStat` struct

https://github.com/golang/go/blob/03845e30f7b73d1703bd8c21017297f6eecb76d6/src/os/types_windows.go#L353-L363

`loadFileId` sees that fs.path is an empty string and returns before setting `fs.vol`, `fs.idxhi`, and `fs.idxlo`

https://github.com/golang/go/blob/03845e30f7b73d1703bd8c21017297f6eecb76d6/src/os/types_windows.go#L287-L293

This is explained here

https://github.com/golang/go/blob/03845e30f7b73d1703bd8c21017297f6eecb76d6/src/os/types_windows.go#L75-L77

Now the `vol`, `idxhi`, and `idxlo` fields have never been set, so they will always be 0 for any character file or pipe, so any two character files or pipes will always claim to be the same file.

As far as I know there isn't a way on Windows to determine if two character files or pipes are the same, since [GetFileInformationByHandle](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-getfileinformationbyhandle) can't be called on these types of files. If someone more familiar with the Windows API than me knows better I'd be gladly corrected. But I definitely don't think returning `true` is the correct thing to do here. It seems that the convention is that when `os.SameFile` returns `true` that is a guarantee that the two files are the same, but when it returns `false` that doesn't guarantee that they are distinct. I think ideally there would be a function that could tell you whether two files were definitely the same, definitely distinct, or whether their distinctness could not be determined, but that's not what we have, unfortunately

As far as I know this bug has existed since https://github.com/golang/go/commit/ebd67ba588eabd5bf968b5bd14dff21a1a1b1be4 in some form, and has just not been noticed.

A way that I think would fix the issue would be to change

https://github.com/golang/go/blob/03845e30f7b73d1703bd8c21017297f6eecb76d6/src/os/stat_windows.go#L115
to 
```go
return &fileStat{name: filepathlite.Base(name), filetype: ft, path: name}, nil
```
but I don't know if that might cause other issues, of if that's the best approach

title: cmd/compile/internal/ssa: elide redundant 32-bit zero extensions on arm64
content:
ZeroUpper32Bits knows about arm64's W-form ALU results, but not about its
zero-extending loads and register moves. The late lower rule
(MOVWUreg x) && ZeroUpper32Bits(x, 3) => x therefore never fires for a
value that came from MOVWUload/MOVHUload/MOVBUload or from a narrower
MOV*Ureg.

With a single use the extension still folds away, via
(MOVWUreg x:(MOVWUload _ _)) => (MOVDreg x) and
(MOVDreg x) && x.Uses == 1 => (MOVDnop x). With a second consumer -- a
loaded uint32 field used both as a slice index and in a bounds compare,
the regexp onepass shape -- the MOVDreg survives as a real MOVD Rx,Ry
register copy.

Add the arm64 zero-extending loads and register moves to
ZeroUpper32Bits, mirroring the byte and halfword op lists that CL 804064
adds to ZeroUpper56Bits and ZeroUpper48Bits. The two changes are
independent; this one applies on its own.

Measured at 7b4aab82eb with go build -a -gcflags=-S std at
GOARCH=arm64: 117 fewer register copies (runtime -36, regexp -26,
internal/zstd -11, internal/coverage/cformat -8) for -592 bytes of
function text across 26 packages, with a single-copy regression in
errors.

Updates #43357
author: andig

title: cmd/go: Regression in Go 1.26 due to new pkg-config flag validation from #77387 banning safe `--define-variable` values
content:
### Go version

go version go1.26.3 linux/amd64

### Output of `go env` in your module/workspace:

```shell
n/a
```

### What did you do?

Upgrade from Go 1.25 to Go 1.26

### What did you see happen?

An existing build started failing with:
```
foobar/core/foobar/protocol/foobar/common: invalid flag in pkg-config: --define-variable=srcdir=/home/tcagent3/opt/teamcity/work/tech-build/foobar/tech/core/foobar/protocol/foobar/common (see https://go.dev/s/invalidflag)
```

Upon investigation, it seems that the fix for #77387 has resulted in banning safe flag values in pkg-config files, namely those that define variables with values containing dash characters, amongst others.

I am guessing that the regex at https://github.com/golang/go/blob/2403e594a5b279bd7b393c32f74528fd4ef29c4a/src/cmd/go/internal/work/security.go#L262 was intended to be something slightly different.

The outcome is that I am no longer able to build this (internal) software without ensuring there is no dash character anywhere in the absolute pathname containing the build environment, though other users may be impacted in other ways depending on the purpose for which they were using variables.

### What did you expect to see?

No regression.

title: proposal: cmd/go: add -doctool flag to specify alternative doc servers or pkgsite versions
content:
### Proposal Details

Currently, `go doc -http` serves local HTML documentation using a fixed, hardcoded version of pkgsite
(golang.org/x/pkgsite/cmd/internal/doc). This proposal adds a `-doctool` flag to `go doc` allowing users to specify a custom local documentation server binary or dynamically fetch a different pkgsite version.

```bash
go doc -http -doctool <spec> ...
```
## Background

When previewing docs with `go doc -http`, developers and tooling authors often need to:
1. Test against newer or older versions of pkgsite (e.g., `@latest` or `@v1.2.3`).
2. Serve docs using the local build of pkgsite (for testing or bug fix) or company-internal documentation rendering servers.

Other `go` commands already support tool-override flags using a pattern, such as `go vet -vettool=prog` and `go fix -fixtool=prog`.

## Spec

This flag is used only with `-http`. The flag accepts two types of arguments:

1. Alternative version or package (`@version` or `<modulepath>@version`):
   Shorthands like `@latest`, `v1.2.3`, `latest`, or explicit module paths (e.g., `example.com/mypkgsite@v1.0.0`). `go doc` dynamically builds and runs the specified package.

2. Local binary:
   A local file path or binary name (e.g., `-doctool=./mydoc` or `-doctool=$(which customdoc)`). Following the exact same logic as `-vettool` and `-fixtool`, the path is resolved using `filepath.Abs` before any `-C` directory changes and validated prior to execution.

## Compatibility

This change is fully backwards compatible. If `-doctool` is omitted, `go doc -http` continues using the default built-in pkgsite version.

title: cmd/go,testing: support stopping fuzzing after coverage plateaus
content:
### Go version

go version go1.25.x linux/amd64

### Output of `go env` in your module/workspace:

```shell
Not available at the moment. I can provide the full `go env` output later if needed.
```

### What did you do?

### What version of Go are you using?

go version go1.25.x

### Does this issue reproduce with the latest release?

Yes.

### What did you do?

The built-in Go fuzzer currently supports stopping after a fixed duration using `-fuzztime`.

In practice, during long-running fuzzing campaigns, coverage often reaches a plateau long before the configured timeout expires.

For example:

- coverage grows during the first several minutes;
- afterwards no new interesting inputs or coverage are found for tens of minutes or even hours;
- the fuzzer continues consuming CPU until `-fuzztime` expires.

This is especially noticeable in CI and Kubernetes-based fuzzing infrastructure where CPU time is limited.

This is not a new fuzzing concept. AFL++ provides a similar mechanism through the `AFL_EXIT_ON_TIME` environment variable:

> `AFL_EXIT_ON_TIME` causes afl-fuzz to terminate if no new paths were found within a specified period of time (in seconds). May be convenient for some types of automated jobs.

Reference:
https://aflplus.plus/docs/env_variables/#settings-for-afl-fuzz

### What did you expect to see?

It would be useful to have a stopping condition based on coverage progress rather than only elapsed time.

For example:

```text
go test -fuzz=FuzzFoo -fuzzplateau=10m
```

where the fuzzer exits if no new coverage has been discovered for 10 minutes.

Alternatively, exposing coverage progress or "new coverage discovered" events through an API or statistics would allow external orchestrators to implement their own stopping policy without introducing a new command-line flag.

### What did you see instead?

Currently the only built-in stopping condition is elapsed time (`-fuzztime`), so fuzzing continues even when coverage has not changed for a long period.

### What did you see happen?

The built-in Go fuzzer currently supports stopping only after a fixed duration using `-fuzztime`.

In practice, coverage often reaches a plateau long before the configured timeout expires. After that point, the fuzzer may continue running for tens of minutes or even hours without discovering new coverage while continuing to consume CPU resources.

This is especially noticeable in CI pipelines and Kubernetes-based fuzzing infrastructure where compute resources are limited.

A similar concept already exists in AFL++ through the `AFL_EXIT_ON_TIME` environment variable:

> `AFL_EXIT_ON_TIME` causes afl-fuzz to terminate if no new paths were found within a specified period of time (in seconds). May be convenient for some types of automated jobs.

Reference:
https://aflplus.plus/docs/env_variables/#settings-for-afl-fuzz

### What did you expect to see?

It would be useful to provide a way to stop fuzzing after no new coverage has been discovered for a configurable period of time.

For example:

```text
go test -fuzz=FuzzFoo -fuzzplateau=10m
```

Alternatively, exposing coverage progress or notifications about newly discovered coverage would allow external tools to implement the same policy without introducing a dedicated command-line flag.

title: proposal: cmd/go: add `GO$GOARCH=all`
content:
### Proposal Details

You can currently use things like `GOAMD64`, `GOARM64`, ... to indicate to the compiler and assembler that certain optional CPU features are always supported.
it's also possible to use that information in a go program like by using `amd64.v3` tag.

---

This is fairly limited, the defaults are sometime outdated (GOAMD64=v2 is supported by nearly anything still we default to v1).
This either mean we do not use newer instruction sets, or we waste CPU cycles checking for them at runtime.

Instead I propose `GOAMD64=all` (and others). This would build the program with all levels; then before the binary start the dynamic loader patch the binary to use the best supported level on the current CPU.
Most functions compile no differently between v1, v2, ... thus theses can be deduped by the linker.

title: proposal: cmd/go: add FileHashes to go list -json output
content:
I think this is one of perhaps a few missing features that can unlock greater reliability in `go`<->`gopls` interop.

### Background

Tools that consume `go list -json` (notably gopls, via `go/packages`) receive file lists (`GoFiles`, `CompiledGoFiles`, etc.) but have no way to know what the go command actually saw in those files. Between the time `go list` reads a file and the time the tool reads it, the content may change. This makes it impossible to detect whether information derived from `go list -export` or `-compiled` is coherent with the source the tool subsequently parses.

gopls in particular wants to detect this incoherence so it can re-invoke the go command rather than present stale or inconsistent results.

The existing `BuildID` field (#37281) is a related package-level witness, but it is salted with the toolchain version and folds in flags and transitive dependencies, so it changes when source files do not; it also requires `-export`. A per-file, unsalted content hash is the missing complement.

### Proposal

Prototype in [CL 768880](https://go-review.googlesource.com/c/go/+/768880).

Add a new field to the `Package` struct reported by `go list`:

	// FileHashes maps each source file listed above to the hex-encoded
	// SHA-256 hash of its contents at the time go list read it.
	FileHashes map[string]string

The map key is the file name exactly as it appears in the corresponding file list (relative to `Dir` for source files, absolute for generated `CompiledGoFiles`). The value is the lowercase hex encoding of the SHA-256 digest. Files that cannot be opened are omitted.

The field is populated only when explicitly requested via `-json=FileHashes` (or referenced from `-f`). It covers all files reported in the source-file lists, including test and ignored files.

When `-overlay` is in effect, the hash is of the overlay content.

### Cost

When `go list` is invoked with `-compiled`, `-export`, or a request for `Stale`, the build action graph already computes the SHA-256 of every input file (cmd/go/internal/work.buildActionID, via `cache.FileHash`) to form the cache key. In those modes—precisely the modes `go/packages` uses when type information is needed—reporting `FileHashes` adds no additional I/O or hashing; it is a map lookup per file.

When none of those flags is set, requesting `FileHashes` requires reading each file in full (the package loader otherwise reads only the file header through the import block). This is an opt-in cost paid only by callers that ask for the field.

### Compatibility

This adds a field; existing consumers are unaffected. The `-json=field,...` selector means the field is never computed or emitted unless requested.

CC @matloob @adonovan

title: proposal: cmd/go: tell tools they are being run via `go tool`
content:
### Proposal Details

## Summary

`go tool` set environment variable(s) that allows a tool to identify being run from `go tool`.

## Proposal

When `go tool` executes a tool, set the following variables:
* `GOTOOL=<tool import path>`
* `GOTOOLMOD=<go.mod used by "go tool -modfile">` to allow recursive call to `go tool` with another tool from the same go.mod (details in #79449 )
* `GOTOOLVERSION=<module version of the tool>` if not the main module (see also #75033 which is about [`runtime/debug.BuildInfo`](https://pkg.go.dev/runtime/debug#BuildInfo) for tools)

As a tool being called by `go tool` might itself call another tool via `go tool`, all `go tool` specific environment variables of a parent tool execution must be overwritten or deleted.

## Rationale

Tools can currently run in two modes:
* _stand-alone_: when installed with `go install <tool>@<version>` and executed as normal commands from the shell
* _module tool_: when declared in go.mod and executed through `go tool <tool>`

To improve integration of tools with the Go toolchain, I think that tools should be able to distinguish in which mode they are being executed: when running _stand-alone_, they should be able to detect if they are working in a Go module which has declared them, and then work just as a shim that delegate to `go tool` to the specific version selected for the project is executed.

The purpose of this proposal is to help the tool to distinguish if it is being executed via `go tool` (_stand-alone_ vs _module tool_ as defined above).

For example `golang.org/x/tools/cmd/stringer` installed with `go install` should be able to detect that it is executed from a Go module that has `golang.org/x/tools/cmd/stringer` declared (and so locked to a specific version), and then forward its arguments to `go tool golang.org/x/tools/cmd/stringer`. But to avoid infinite recursion, `stringer` should be able to discover if it is already running via `go tool`.

_Update 2026-05-18: fixed Markdown for specification of environment variable values as `<bla bla>` was hidden_

title: cmd/go: `go build` running `hg pull -f` in mercurial repository resulting in passphrase prompt
content:
### Go version

go version go1.26.2 linux/amd64

### Output of `go env` in your module/workspace:

```shell
AR='ar'

GOHOSTARCH='amd64'

GOVCS=''
GOVERSION='go1.26.2'
GOWORK=''
PKG_CONFIG='pkg-config'
```

### What did you do?

I have a project contained in a mercurial repository. When running `go build` it executes `hg pull -f` which triggers a prompt requesting credentials. This is a bit annoying. Also I do not want a go build to have such side effects. This is totally unexpected. 

### What did you see happen?

```
xxx@xxx:~/Projects/gemma$ go build -x -o ./cmd/gemma/gemma ./cmd/gemma
WORK=/tmp/go-build3922253331
cd /home/xxx/Projects/gemma
hg log -r. -T {node}:{date|hgdate}
cd /home/xxx/Projects/gemma
hg status -S
cd /home/xxx/Projects/gemma; hg pull -f
Enter passphrase for key '/home/xxx/.ssh/id_rsa':
```

### What did you expect to see?

This behavior was introduced in go 1.26.0. We verified that this does not happen in go 1.25.x. This seems to be related to https://github.com/golang/go/commit/426ef30ecf2d2b6eadd962358884ed68220b9cc5 (#75119). 

I do not expect a go build to run `hg pull -f` in my project.

title: document #[global_allocator] constraints
content:
<!-- homu-ignore:start -->
*[View all comments](https://triagebot.infra.rust-lang.org/gh-comments/rust-lang/rust/pull/159720)*
<!-- homu-ignore:end -->

`#[global_allocator]` is opsem magic. For instance, even if we do
```rust
use std::alloc::System;

#[global_allocator]
static ALLOC: System = System;
```
it is still UB to allocate via `std::alloc::alloc()` and deallocate via `System.dealloc()`. This is because we add special magic LLVM attributes in the `#[global_allocator]` machinery that tell LLVM about our global allocation methods so it can optimize accordingly, and mixing allocators is against those rules.

Cc @rust-lang/opsem @rust-lang/lang @nia-e @maxdexh
@nikic is this enough to ensure that adding your intrinsics is sound?

title: llvm.dbg.value should be used instead of llvm.dbg.declare wherever possible.
content:
*(I'm opening this issue because I can't find a pre-existing one)*

`llvm.dbg.declare` describes the location in memory of a debuginfo variable, whereas `llvm.dbg.value` describes the value itself directly. Today we only use the former, which means that in debug mode, all named variables are placed on the stack, even if they're simple scalars (e.g. integers).

Ideally, we'd use `llvm.dbg.value` in the same situations where we skip creating a stack slot (e.g. LLVM `alloca`), i.e. for scalars, vectors and pairs of scalars.

<hr/>

However, this is much harder than I expected, mostly due to LLVM being too eager to throw away `llvm.dbg.value` if computing the value can be avoided (i.e. it's not used by anything else).

I think `llvm.dbg.declare` *only* fares better because at `opt-level=0`, the lack of SROA means `alloca`s are kept around pretty much completely intact.

`FastISel` (used at `opt-level=0`) [throws away any non-trivial `llvm.dbg.value`](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/30a8865142abe309bb9aceede2708c171a2904ea/llvm/lib/CodeGen/SelectionDAG/FastISel.cpp#L1445-L1446), but disabling it with `-C llvm-args=-fast-isel=0` only helps some simple cases (such as a reference to another stack variable - IMO `FastISel` should be improved to handle those, I don't see why it couldn't).

In general, it looks like Instruction Selection ("`ISel`") in LLVM ignores `llvm.dbg.value`s while building all of the machine instructions for a BB, and only *afterwards* does it come back to the `llvm.dbg.value`s and lower them to `DBG_VALUE`, using the value *only* if it already exists (i.e. something else needs that same value, at runtime), and otherwise it leads to `<optimized out>` vars.

Maybe the upcoming `GlobalISel` approach handles `llvm.dbg.value` better, but I would need to target `AArch64` to even try it out, from what I hear (I might still do it out of curiosity).

<hr/>

While investigating this I also came across https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/8855#discussion_r374392128 - but setting `AlwaysPreserve` to `true` only keeps the debuginfo variable around, it doesn't help at all with keeping any value alive (so you end up with `<optimized out>` in the debugger, instead of the variable missing).

I haven't seen anything that would make `llvm.dbg.value` keep the value alive so it's guaranteed to be available to the debugger, but if there is such a thing, it's probably the way to go, if we want to avoid relying on the stack so much.

cc @nikomatsakis @michaelwoerister @hanna-kruppe

title: Add `lldb-repr` command for `tests/debuginfo`
content:
<!-- homu-ignore:start -->
*[View all comments](https://triagebot.infra.rust-lang.org/gh-comments/rust-lang/rust/pull/158298)*
<!-- homu-ignore:end -->

Very much so a work in progress, but there's a bunch of stuff that probably needs discussing, so I figured I'd start that up now.

To recap, the control flow is as follows:

1. `lldb-repr` is automatically split into, essentially `lldb-command:repr var` + `lldb-check:var: Ok`
2. the relevant target, bless state, paths, etc. are passed to the LLDB command via env vars
3. The lldb command runs `lldb_batchmode.main()`
4. the input commands are executed line by line.
5. If the command is a `repr` pseudo-command, it is intercepted and passed to the checking logic
5a. if blessing, `INPUT_DATA` is blank. Each check inserts the appropriate var into `INPUT_DATA`, and then runs the checking logic against `INPUT_DATA` as normal (for sanity reasons)
5b. the checking logic checks the variable against `INPUT_DATA` (<-- this is incomplete atm, see below for what still isn't finished) and prints any mismatches that occur.
6. Once all commands have been run (or if a `quit`/`exit` command is encountered) `lldb_batchmode` checks 1. have we seen every type that exists in the input data? 2. have we seen every variable that exists in the input data? If not, it reports what was missing and exits with an error code. 
6a. If `--bless`, and no errors occurred, and at least 1 `repr` pseudo-command was processed, `INPUT_DATA` is serialized and written to the input data file.

To preemptively answer the question "When blessing, why not just build a second `TargetData` instance and compare `INPUT_DATA` to that?" - the goal of diffing in python (rather than rust) is to still have access to the underlying LLDB objects for error reporting purposes. 

<details>
<summary>Sample Output (`basic-types.rs`)</summary>
The input data was manually tampered with to force errors (`char32_t` size set to 1, double type renamed to `half`, `int` type deleted)

```txt
error: Error while running LLDB
status: exit status: 1
... # skipping to repr output for brevity
repr b
b: Ok
repr i
i: Ok
repr c
  [repr error: type 'char32_t'] size does not match.
    Expected: '1'
    Got: '4'
repr i8
i8: Ok
repr i16
i16: Ok
repr i32
i32: Ok
repr i64
i64: Ok
repr u
u: Ok
repr u8
u8: Ok
repr u16
u16: Ok
repr u32
  [repr error: type 'unsigned int'] type not found in input data
repr u64
u64: Ok
repr f32
f32: Ok
repr f64
  [repr error: type 'double'] type not found in input data
[repr error] The following types were expected, but were not tested:
  {'half'}
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>Sample Output (`simple-struct.rs`)</summary>
The input data was manually tampered with to force errors.

* `simple_struct::NoPadding64` field name `y` to `q`
* `simple_struct::NoPadding163264` last field moved to first position
* `simple_struct::InternalPadding` `y` field deleted
* `simple_struct::PaddingAtEnd` `q` field added

Keep in mind that I edited the *expected* data, not the actual structs in the test file, so the output reports the opposite of the changes i made (sortof) i.e. it reports that `q` was deleted because it exists in the expected data but not in the LLDB object.

```txt
repr no_padding16
no_padding16: Ok
repr no_padding32
no_padding32: Ok
repr no_padding64
  [repr error: type 'simple_struct::NoPadding64'] The following field(s) appear to have been renamed. If this is expected,
  consider rerunning with the `--bless` option: 
    ['q -> y']
repr no_padding163264
  [repr error: type 'simple_struct::NoPadding163264'] Field(s) appear to have been rearranged. If this was expected, try re-running with the `--bless` option
    Expected:
[     Field(name='a', type='short', offset=12),
      Field(name='b', type='unsigned short', offset=14),
      Field(name='c', type='int', offset=8),
      Field(name='d', type='unsigned long', offset=0)]
    Got:
[     Field(name='d', type='unsigned long', offset=0),
      Field(name='a', type='short', offset=12),
      Field(name='b', type='unsigned short', offset=14),
      Field(name='c', type='int', offset=8)]
repr internal_padding
  [repr error: type 'simple_struct::InternalPadding'] The following field(s) appear to have been added to the type:
    {Field(name='y', type='long', offset=0)}
repr padding_at_end
  [repr error: type 'simple_struct::PaddingAtEnd'] The following field(s) appear to have been removed from the type:
    {Field(name='q', type='float', offset=12)}
[repr error] The following types were expected, but were not tested:
  {'double', 'long', 'unsigned long'}
```
</details>

The errors are of the form `[repr error <error source>] <error info>`. The errors are slightly indented to make it easier to scan and associate errors with their source. The formatting is 1st draft and largely abstracted away via [these functions](https://github.com/Walnut356/rust/blob/bd4a0c7b80b448778247dda4b203074d58eff64d/src/etc/lldb_batchmode/common.py#L20-L39). We can pretty trivially change how they're formatted by modifying/replacing these functions.

Also, each type in a test is only tested once per test, regardless of how many variables/fields reference it. When a type is seen a second time, if the prior check was a mismatch, it reports that the type does not match and  **does not** repeat the specific error messages of the mismatch. Instead, it directs people to look at the original type error further up in the output. 

# TODO

- [x] Variable child mismatches don't have error reporting
- [x] Rearrange the checks a bit so the type check happens midway through the variable check. Some of the variable's information is useful for the type's error reporting and vice versa.
- [x] use some info from `lldb_providers` and the original `SBValue` and `SBType` to improve error messages 
- [ ] Some sort of warning if the python/lldb version and/or feature flags don't match
- [x] A few more tests with input data to help verify behavior (one with generics, one with a synthetic/summary provider, probably need to enforce a formatter for `u8`/`i8` at some point to test that too).
- [x] Various improvements to the error message wording/information/formatting/consistency.
- [ ] Probably some other stuff i'm forgetting about that I'll add in later

r? @jieyouxu, @Kobzol

raw_json.body:
<!-- homu-ignore:start -->
*[View all comments](https://triagebot.infra.rust-lang.org/gh-comments/rust-lang/rust/pull/158298)*
<!-- homu-ignore:end -->

Very much so a work in progress, but there's a bunch of stuff that probably needs discussing, so I figured I'd start that up now.

To recap, the control flow is as follows:

1. `lldb-repr` is automatically split into, essentially `lldb-command:repr var` + `lldb-check:var: Ok`
2. the relevant target, bless state, paths, etc. are passed to the LLDB command via env vars
3. The lldb command runs `lldb_batchmode.main()`
4. the input commands are executed line by line.
5. If the command is a `repr` pseudo-command, it is intercepted and passed to the checking logic
5a. if blessing, `INPUT_DATA` is blank. Each check inserts the appropriate var into `INPUT_DATA`, and then runs the checking logic against `INPUT_DATA` as normal (for sanity reasons)
5b. the checking logic checks the variable against `INPUT_DATA` (<-- this is incomplete atm, see below for what still isn't finished) and prints any mismatches that occur.
6. Once all commands have been run (or if a `quit`/`exit` command is encountered) `lldb_batchmode` checks 1. have we seen every type that exists in the input data? 2. have we seen every variable that exists in the input data? If not, it reports what was missing and exits with an error code. 
6a. If `--bless`, and no errors occurred, and at least 1 `repr` pseudo-command was processed, `INPUT_DATA` is serialized and written to the input data file.

To preemptively answer the question "When blessing, why not just build a second `TargetData` instance and compare `INPUT_DATA` to that?" - the goal of diffing in python (rather than rust) is to still have access to the underlying LLDB objects for error reporting purposes. 

<details>
<summary>Sample Output (`basic-types.rs`)</summary>
The input data was manually tampered with to force errors (`char32_t` size set to 1, double type renamed to `half`, `int` type deleted)

```txt
error: Error while running LLDB
status: exit status: 1
... # skipping to repr output for brevity
repr b
b: Ok
repr i
i: Ok
repr c
  [repr error: type 'char32_t'] size does not match.
    Expected: '1'
    Got: '4'
repr i8
i8: Ok
repr i16
i16: Ok
repr i32
i32: Ok
repr i64
i64: Ok
repr u
u: Ok
repr u8
u8: Ok
repr u16
u16: Ok
repr u32
  [repr error: type 'unsigned int'] type not found in input data
repr u64
u64: Ok
repr f32
f32: Ok
repr f64
  [repr error: type 'double'] type not found in input data
[repr error] The following types were expected, but were not tested:
  {'half'}
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>Sample Output (`simple-struct.rs`)</summary>
The input data was manually tampered with to force errors.

* `simple_struct::NoPadding64` field name `y` to `q`
* `simple_struct::NoPadding163264` last field moved to first position
* `simple_struct::InternalPadding` `y` field deleted
* `simple_struct::PaddingAtEnd` `q` field added

Keep in mind that I edited the *expected* data, not the actual structs in the test file, so the output reports the opposite of the changes i made (sortof) i.e. it reports that `q` was deleted because it exists in the expected data but not in the LLDB object.

```txt
repr no_padding16
no_padding16: Ok
repr no_padding32
no_padding32: Ok
repr no_padding64
  [repr error: type 'simple_struct::NoPadding64'] The following field(s) appear to have been renamed. If this is expected,
  consider rerunning with the `--bless` option: 
    ['q -> y']
repr no_padding163264
  [repr error: type 'simple_struct::NoPadding163264'] Field(s) appear to have been rearranged. If this was expected, try re-running with the `--bless` option
    Expected:
[     Field(name='a', type='short', offset=12),
      Field(name='b', type='unsigned short', offset=14),
      Field(name='c', type='int', offset=8),
      Field(name='d', type='unsigned long', offset=0)]
    Got:
[     Field(name='d', type='unsigned long', offset=0),
      Field(name='a', type='short', offset=12),
      Field(name='b', type='unsigned short', offset=14),
      Field(name='c', type='int', offset=8)]
repr internal_padding
  [repr error: type 'simple_struct::InternalPadding'] The following field(s) appear to have been added to the type:
    {Field(name='y', type='long', offset=0)}
repr padding_at_end
  [repr error: type 'simple_struct::PaddingAtEnd'] The following field(s) appear to have been removed from the type:
    {Field(name='q', type='float', offset=12)}
[repr error] The following types were expected, but were not tested:
  {'double', 'long', 'unsigned long'}
```
</details>

The errors are of the form `[repr error <error source>] <error info>`. The errors are slightly indented to make it easier to scan and associate errors with their source. The formatting is 1st draft and largely abstracted away via [these functions](https://github.com/Walnut356/rust/blob/bd4a0c7b80b448778247dda4b203074d58eff64d/src/etc/lldb_batchmode/common.py#L20-L39). We can pretty trivially change how they're formatted by modifying/replacing these functions.

Also, each type in a test is only tested once per test, regardless of how many variables/fields reference it. When a type is seen a second time, if the prior check was a mismatch, it reports that the type does not match and  **does not** repeat the specific error messages of the mismatch. Instead, it directs people to look at the original type error further up in the output. 

# TODO

- [x] Variable child mismatches don't have error reporting
- [x] Rearrange the checks a bit so the type check happens midway through the variable check. Some of the variable's information is useful for the type's error reporting and vice versa.
- [x] use some info from `lldb_providers` and the original `SBValue` and `SBType` to improve error messages 
- [ ] Some sort of warning if the python/lldb version and/or feature flags don't match
- [x] A few more tests with input data to help verify behavior (one with generics, one with a synthetic/summary provider, probably need to enforce a formatter for `u8`/`i8` at some point to test that too).
- [x] Various improvements to the error message wording/information/formatting/consistency.
- [ ] Probably some other stuff i'm forgetting about that I'll add in later

r? @jieyouxu, @Kobzol

title: Split non-local `semicolon_in_expressions_from_macros` into a separate lint
content:
The new handling for non-local macros in
`semicolon_in_expressions_from_macros` produces new deny-by-default
lints on various existing crates, which have not previously received
warnings because prior Rust versions suppressed them. Split those out
into a new `semicolon_in_expressions_from_non_local_macros` lint, and
make that one warn-by-default (and FCW warn-in-deps), rather than
deny-by-default, to give the ecosystem time to adapt.

This reintroduces the `is_local` tracking from commit
9192337331dc8c59c6367d316c32f08f975b7140.
author: joshtriplett

the existing `clang/gcc` checks don't match on systems where `self.cc(target)` resolves to `cc`, so `-fdebug-prefix-map` isn't forwarded to the `C` compiler.

this leaves local checkout paths in `compiler-builtins DWARF`.
recognize cc as well so the remapping flag is forwarded. confirmed `remap-path-prefix-std passes`, and inspecting the generated `DWARF` to verify that checkout paths are remapped.

title: rustdoc: warn on improperly interleaved HTML/MD
content:
<!-- homu-ignore:start -->
*[View all comments](https://triagebot.infra.rust-lang.org/gh-comments/rust-lang/rust/pull/158709)*
<!-- homu-ignore:end -->

Enhances the `rustdoc::invalid_html_tags` lint to warn in cases where pulldown-cmark will produce invalid HTML because the Markdown and HTML are improperly nested.

As an extreme example, this code does not do what it looks like it does, and it doesn't produce a warning under current nightly, either:

```markdown
Figure 1: an X
<svg viewBox="0 0 10 10">
<path
    d="M0 10L10 0M10 10L0 0"
    stroke="black"
>
</svg>
```

This pull request makes it warn:

```text
error: unopened HTML tag `svg`
  --> $DIR/invalid-html-tags.rs:285:5
   |
LL | /// <svg viewBox="0 0 10 10">
   |     ---- does not match this unclosed tag
...
LL | /// >
   |     - because the Markdown paragraph is interrupted by this block quote
LL | /// </svg>
   |     ^^^^^^ this unopened tag
```

See also: https://talk.commonmark.org/t/thoughts-on-changing-supported-html-syntax-to-include-the-dangling-closing-angle-bracket/3827
author: notriddle

title: API: Ability dismiss own showInformationMessage/showErrorMessage
content:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
Please add ability dismiss own messages.

Here is a use case:
Show error/information message when user entered none-existent path in the settings and remove the message when path is correct.
Yes, we can specify `type: "uri"` for the setting, but this will not allow user to leave the field blank or enter relative paths.

This will also allow us to create temporary messages that would hide themselves after some time.

Currently we can force to close all currently displaying messages by displaying same message 4 times in a short period of time, but that's just a hack that can't be used to dismiss one specific message.

title: Agent auto-persists referenceable/feature-specific knowledge into always-loaded global memory, inflating per-turn context cost
content:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.x (current, June 2026)
- VS Code Version: 1.127.x
- OS Version: Windows 11
- Feature: agent mode — memory tool (auto-write behavior)
- Selected model: Claude (Opus/Sonnet class)
- Logs: see measured evidence below

### Shared context (this issue has a sibling: #323167)
Both this issue and #323167 stem from the memory feature operating silently/automatically. The auto-write behavior described here continually grows /memories/ files, and the corruption bug in #323167 then multiplies that content — so the two compound each other (silent context bloat + data corruption).

### Core defect
In agent mode the model auto-persists **feature-specific and already-referenceable knowledge** into **always-loaded global memory** (`/memories/`). The first ~200 lines of user/global memory are injected into context on **every turn, in every workspace**, indefinitely. This is the wrong storage tier for this kind of content, for three reasons:

1. **Duplication of referenceable knowledge.** Feature details that already live in retrievable `docs/` files (or repo memory) get copied into always-loaded memory. The same information that a one-time on-demand `read_file` could supply *only when relevant* is instead injected into context on every turn forever. Same data, loaded continuously instead of on access — negative value.

2. **No relevance scoping.** Global memory loads in every workspace regardless of topic. A partner servicing N customers ends up loading, in customer X's sessions, customer Y's feature notes. Even within a single app, knowledge for feature A is loaded while working on unrelated feature B.

3. **Unbounded time cost.** A feature you don't touch for 3–4 years is still loaded on every turn in the interim, with zero corresponding use, and nothing ages it out.

### The principle being violated
Always-loaded persistent memory should hold only **small, cross-cutting, non-referenceable** facts (durable preferences, hard-won gotchas). Anything that is **(a) already retrievable from a doc, or (b) feature/workspace-specific** should NOT be auto-written to global memory — it should stay in `docs/` (or at most repo-scoped, on-demand memory) and be pulled only when relevant. The current `<memoryInstructions>` ("record what you learned") pushes the agent to do the opposite.

### Reproduced cross-workspace leak (captured this session)
I have a multi-root setup with separate workspaces. One workspace contains **only** a Business Central (AL) app and has **no knowledge of, and no files from, a separate React Native mobile app**. From that BC-only workspace I asked the agent — explicitly forbidding it from searching or reading any files — what it knew about the mobile app's PO-extraction work.

It answered with mobile/Python-pipeline feature specifics (`operating_pressure_psi` as a per-`part_item` schema field, the Phase A/B/C structure, a "mobile applier" that reads `shipping_resolved.agent_code/service_code` and falls back to `carrierHint`/`serviceLevelHint` on `csr_confirm`) and **explicitly attributed all of it to an auto-loaded global memory note**, `PO-Extract-Phase2-Handoff.md`. Verbatim from its reply:

> "Where the knowledge came from: Entirely from my persistent user-memory file … specifically the auto-loaded note `PO-Extraction-Phase2-Handoff.md` (under user memory). Nothing here came from reading the workspace, `app/docs/`, or any `.ts`/`.tsx` file in this session."

Notably it also correctly declined to fabricate the parts the note didn't contain — so the attribution is credible, not a hallucination. This is a concrete demonstration that feature-specific notes from one workspace are loaded into an unrelated workspace's context, with zero relevance to the task at hand.

### Measured evidence (real machine, single user)
- User/global memory: 26,438 bytes ≈ 6,610 tokens, auto-loaded every turn, every workspace
- Much of it is feature-specific content that already exists in this repo's `docs/` (e.g. PO-extraction internals) — i.e. duplicated, not unique
- All memory across all workspaces: 24 files, 156,069 bytes ≈ 39,017 tokens
- Example of mis-tiered content: workspace-specific feature notes (`phys-inv-*`, `PO-Extract-*`) auto-written to globally-loaded memory rather than left in retrievable docs

### Cost / impact (corrected — important)
The primary cost on a **GitHub Copilot subscription is NOT direct dollars.** Copilot meters by **premium request, not tokens** — one prompt in agent mode = one premium request × the model's multiplier, with tool calls and autonomous steps excluded, and overage billed per request ($0.04/request). Token volume inside a request does not change the billed amount. So on Copilot the real cost of this bloat is:

- **Context-window dilution and answer-quality degradation** — every turn spends a fixed slice of the window on irrelevant, often duplicated, cross-workspace notes.
- **Compounding with #323167** — corrupted/duplicated memory enlarges that always-loaded slice further.

The dollar cost only materializes under **per-token billing (Anthropic API / BYOK)**. As an order-of-magnitude reference there: ~6,610 tokens × ~420 sessions/month ≈ ~2.8M input tokens/month; at an Opus-class list rate of roughly $15 / 1M input tokens that is on the order of ~$40/month — but this does NOT apply to a standard Copilot subscription, where the same usage is $0 at the margin.

### Requests
1. **Stop auto-persisting referenceable/feature-specific content to always-loaded memory.** Prefer leaving it in `docs/` (or on-demand repo memory) and reading it only when relevant. Reserve global memory for small, cross-cutting facts.
2. **Relevance-scope what is loaded** — don't inject every workspace's notes into every other workspace's context.
3. **Age out / cap** stale entries, and surface the memory store's size and context footprint in the UI.
4. Allow `copilot-instructions.md` / project config to suppress or constrain memory writes (ref #308669).
5. (Secondary) make global memory writes opt-in or per-write confirmable.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Use agent mode normally over several sessions with the memory tool available, in a multi-root / multi-workspace setup.
2. Observe that feature-specific notes — content that already exists in retrievable `docs/` — are auto-written to `/memories/` without an explicit request to "save this."
3. From an unrelated workspace, ask the agent (forbidding file reads) about a feature that only exists in another workspace; it will recite it from auto-loaded global memory and attribute it to that note.

### Related
- #323167 — memory file corruption (recursive self-duplication) that enlarges this always-loaded slice
- #308669 — `<memoryInstructions>` cannot be overridden by copilot-instructions.md
